# Axocoatl — a local-first harness for coding agents
> Axocoatl v1.1: the harness you can trust to run coding agents on your own machine or infrastructure. Isolation built in, a complete record of every step, any model, local or hosted.

Axocoatl v1.1 is an Apache-2.0, local-first harness for coding agents working in
real repositories. One Rust executable runs a daemon that executes the Agents and a
browser workbench. Open a repository and work in a
durable, folder-anchored Session: conversation stays at the center while Files,
Source Control, Preview, Terminal, History, Agent activity, and Settings open
around it.

- Isolation built in: every Session's repository tools (file, shell, terminal) run
  in a rootless Podman container (E2B Cloud is an explicit remote option on the
  compatibility path); the web and MCP tools run on the host, and the browser tools
  in a container of their own. Read-only helpers cannot write files: they get no
  file-writing tools and the kernel blocks their shell from writing, creating,
  renaming or deleting repository files or opening TCP connections (Landlock, Linux
  6.7 or later); otherwise they get no shell. Run as root, or on macOS, that shell
  can still change permission bits and timestamps. Per-Agent write scopes share one checkout, and every change is
  checked against complete, digest-verified snapshots taken before and after the
  Agent's work. For an Agent with a shell that check is review evidence, not
  confinement. Container network access is on by default.
- A complete record: required checks run by the host on the exact final files;
  budgets a person approves, charged with what each model call actually used and
  carried across restarts; a durable record of every model call, tool call, budget
  decision and check.
- Any model, per Agent: local models through Ollama and hosted models through
  OpenRouter in native Sessions, each Agent with its own provider and model, so a
  local writer can be reviewed by a stronger model. Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and
  Mistral adapters remain on the compatibility path.

The default team is Lead, an Agent that edits files, and two read-only helpers it
can `delegate` to: Scout answers questions about the code and Reviewer reviews a
change. A new Session starts with Lead alone; the helpers are opt-in. Each helper starts in an empty conversation and returns its answer to the
lead; several can run at once. A team can add required checks, commands the host
runs after the Agents finish, and a required review, a read-only reviewer the host
runs for a bounded number of rounds. The turn completes only when they pass on the
exact final tree. Both are opt-in.

Every Agent runs under a grant with limits a person approves. Each accepted Turn
records its request and context before execution, then keeps every activation,
tool call, budget decision, Agent output, and final lifecycle state in durable
History. Source Control separately shows the repository as it exists now;
Axocoatl does not make a commit or push unless the user deliberately asks for
that Git action.

## What we measured

<!-- measured: axocoatl-1.1.0 2026-10-01 -->
A pre-registered benchmark of 6 Python maintenance tasks (frozen 2026-09-22), scored
by 25 withheld tests the agents never see; writer qwen3-coder 30B running locally,
one run per task, temperature 0. Through Axocoatl 1.1.0, one Agent passed 17/25; the
same writer with a Required review by a stronger local model (gpt-oss 120B) passed
19/25 at 2.6x the tokens. The reviewer reported 15 defects, 14 of them real; the writer
applied the one false alarm too, which cost a test. In a plain agent loop on the same
tasks, more looks by the same model added nothing: self-review 17/25 at 3.5x, a fresh
same-model reviewer 17/25 at 2.3x (it approved every change), while the stronger
reviewer reached 20/25 at 3.3x.
<!-- /measured -->

Extra tokens helped when they bought a stronger model's judgment, not more looks from
the same model. Axocoatl does not claim the default team beats a single Agent, and
one Agent remains the cheaper choice for small tasks.

## Several Ways

When implementation choices need independent evidence, the same Session can run
one task and repository snapshot several Ways with different Agent/model pairs,
compare them, and Keep one passing result as ordinary uncommitted Git changes.
Native Ways retain bounded comparison evidence and the human decision after
cleanup, under explicit storage limits.

## Start

```bash
# Install the checksum-verified axocoatl executable on supported macOS or glibc Linux.
curl -fsSL https://axocoatl.ai/install.sh | sh

# Configure Axocoatl once for this OS user, check host prerequisites, and run.
axocoatl onboard
axocoatl doctor
axocoatl dev
```

Open the sign-in link `axocoatl dev` prints (or run `axocoatl url`). The default
listener is loopback-only, and its API requires a per-daemon token.

The installed executable includes the CLI, Rust daemon, HTTP/WebSocket API, and
workbench browser assets. Those assets are embedded, so using Axocoatl requires no
separate frontend install or bundled browser runtime. Rootless Podman remains the
local sandbox requirement for repository Sessions.

Install from Cargo instead with `cargo install axocoatl-cli` and Rust 1.88 or
newer. Native Windows is not a release target; Windows users run Axocoatl through
WSL2.

## Product model

- **Workspace**: a durable, named identity for one authorized project directory.
- **Session**: one durable work item and conversation inside a Workspace.
- **Turn**: one accepted request, immutable context references, output, bounded
  tool evidence, and final lifecycle state in canonical Session History.
- **Attempt**: one candidate solution. When uncertainty warrants it, a Session
  can explore several isolated Ways and compare their Outcome, Route, available
  diff, Checks, known usage and cost, and optional Judge evidence.
- **Keep this one**: return one passing, non-empty Way to the primary Session
  checkout as an ordinary uncommitted Git change for review.

The ordinary path is the lead and its helpers, or one Agent, in one Session.
Exploring several Ways is optional decision support, not the default interaction model.
The current Ways boundary requires an autonomous single-Agent Session and local Podman; Session
attachments, MCP tools, Skills, and web search are withheld from attempts.

## Runtime underneath

A Rust daemon supervises configured Agent actors and owns the canonical Session
ledger, checkpoint recovery, memory, provider adapters, tool execution, typed
events, Automations, and sandbox lifecycle.

- Native providers: reviewed Ollama profiles and eligible OpenRouter-credit
  text/tool endpoints with whole-call limits. BYOK remains deferred. Direct OpenAI,
  Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, and other compatible adapters retain their supported
  compatibility execution paths.
- Tools: bounded built-ins plus approved tools discovered from configured stdio
  or streamable-HTTP MCP servers. Axocoatl can also expose Agents through its MCP
  server command.
- Native workspace knowledge: versioned Markdown notes, typed links, source hashes,
  proposals, and accepted publication. Sessions in the same Workspace share the
  notes; conversation and exact activation history remain separate. The Knowledge
  inspector exposes notes, evidence, a graph, and a bounded source index. Rust,
  JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, and Python parsing provides definitions and import
  syntax, not complete reference or call-graph resolution.
- Compatibility memory: append-only daily logs, editable core-memory blocks,
  and on-device semantic recall remain distinct from native workspace knowledge.
  Checkpoints are execution-recovery caches; canonical History is the product record.
- Automations: explicit durable graphs configured and reviewed in Settings,
  with manual, interval, event, or Skill triggers and separate run history.
- Lead and helpers: in a native Session, an Agent approved to delegate hands a
  self-contained task to a read-only helper template and waits for its answer.
  The helper's limits are reserved from the lead's grant. Read-only helpers get no
  file-writing tools; their shell runs under Linux Landlock with no repository
  writes and no TCP where Linux 6.7 or later allows it, and otherwise they get no shell.
- Write scopes: an Agent limited to some paths has file tools that refuse other
  paths, and its changes are checked after it finishes. For an Agent with a shell,
  that check is review evidence, not confinement.
- Small local models: an Ollama stream that ends early is retried once, older
  tool output is replaced by a placeholder in later requests, and a request that
  would overflow the context window is trimmed instead of failing.
- Events: the event feed carries the events Skills publish to Automation
  triggers, webhooks, and observers; it is not the Session, Agent graph, Ways
  model, or Automation graph.

## Isolation and network boundary

Rootless Podman is the local sandbox default and supplies native repository
process supervision. E2B Cloud remains an explicit remote option on supported
compatibility paths; native Sessions reject unsupported remote ownership. A local Workspace remains a read-write host bind
inside its sandbox, so the boundary limits repository tools; it is not a defense
against an authorized tool making an unwanted change within that Workspace.

Axocoatl adds no product telemetry, hosted control plane, or Axocoatl account.
Local-first does not mean every configured path is offline. Hosted model
providers, MCP servers, web search and `web_fetch`, webhooks, the optional E2B
Cloud sandbox, Podman image pulls, package downloads and repository traffic, the
hosts declared for the browser tool and the downloads `axocoatl browser install`
makes, requests the daemon sends on egress routes, and the one-time Hugging Face
embedding-model download can use the network. Container network access is on by
default (`sandbox.network: bridge`); set `sandbox.network: none` for repositories
you don't trust. `none` blocks code and commands inside the local Podman sandbox,
turns off native Sessions' `web_search` and `web_fetch`, and leaves the browser only
the app under test; the daemon's other integrations remain separate paths.

## Selected interfaces

```text
axocoatl onboard                 Configure Axocoatl for this OS user
axocoatl doctor                  Environment and dependency checks
axocoatl validate <config>       Validate configuration
axocoatl dev | serve             Run the daemon and browser product
axocoatl url                     Print the browser sign-in link
axocoatl chat -a <agent>         Compatibility terminal chat
axocoatl workflow list | run     Compatibility view/run for Automations
axocoatl agents list|status|restart
axocoatl tokens report
axocoatl mcp servers|tools
```

The browser product has one interactive route at `/`. The HTTP and WebSocket APIs
remain available for integrations; the authoritative route reference is in the
documentation.
